The vault locks the moment the screen turns off; the key is wiped from memory. As long as the screen stays on, you are not asked for the password or fingerprint again.\n\nEntries marked \"Use on the keyboard without a password\" can be used while the vault is locked too; you can turn that mark on and off from each entry\'s own screen.
⚠ This PIN was set up in an older version and is incompatible with this one: entries cannot be opened and the PIN cannot be turned off. Repair it with your master password + PIN.
On: after your fingerprint is read, the PIN is asked. It is not asked when you unlock with the master password — that password is already a strong secret.

Optional. If you turn it on, the fingerprint record is encrypted with the PIN and the PIN is asked after the fingerprint at unlock. Default: off.\nOrder matters: set the PIN first, then enable the fingerprint.

While you use the fingerprint, the master password goes untyped for months and gets forgotten — yet it is also what opens your backups. Once per interval you choose, the password is asked instead of the fingerprint. Default: never.

On. When you tap a sign-in or card form in apps and browsers, your Sekuvo entries appear as a fill option. If the vault is locked, the unlock screen comes first; no value is handed to the system while locked.

If you enable it, tapping a sign-in or card form in apps and browsers offers your Sekuvo entries directly as a fill option. It also offers to save newly entered details to Sekuvo.\n\nThe button below opens system settings. The name of the list that opens varies by device (\"Preferred service\", \"Autofill service\" or \"Passwords, passkeys & autofill\"); just pick Sekuvo from that list.
If you enable the keyboard add-on, you can pick Sekuvo Keyboard from the keyboard switcher in any app and type your saved details straight into the field.
Without this password the backup file CANNOT be opened. Make it DIFFERENT from your master password: the backup password gets typed on computers, the master password never touches a computer.

The PIN must be 4-12 digits. If you forget it, the master password ALONE is not enough — keep the PIN somewhere safe, like your backup password. You have to re-enable the fingerprint afterwards.

resources.string: Choose the app language. It applies to Sekuvo only, not the rest of the phone.
Pick the layouts you actually use. Only the ones you tick appear when you type a secret to a computer — the rest stay out of your way.
At least one layout stays on.

A fully offline vault for passwords, cards and notes. It does not request the Internet permission, so it cannot send your data anywhere — no account, no cloud, no sync, no analytics. Everything is encrypted with AES-256-GCM under a key derived from your master password.
Sekuvo does not collect, transmit or share any data. It is an offline password vault and does not request the Internet permission, so it is technically incapable of sending your data anywhere.
Titles, usernames, passwords, notes and usage history stay on this device, encrypted with a key derived from your master password. Nothing is uploaded, synced or backed up to any server by the app.

Camera — only to scan QR codes you choose to scan, processed on the device.\nBiometrics — only to unlock the vault, through the Android biometric system. Sekuvo never sees or stores your fingerprint or face.\nBluetooth — only when you ask Sekuvo to type a secret into a nearby computer. Only the characters you choose are sent, to the device you paired.

These happen only when you start them. They produce an encrypted file or QR codes protected by a password you set, saved or shown only where you direct them. The app never sends them anywhere on its own.
Sekuvo collects data from no one, including children.
Questions: contact@sekuvo.com\nThe authoritative version of this policy is published at sekuvo.com/privacy/ and is the one that governs in case of any difference.

You set a master password. Everything is encrypted with a key derived from it, so it is the one thing that cannot be recovered — write it somewhere safe.\nComing from another phone? Tap “I have a backup — restore it” on the welcome screen: you still set a master password for this device, then the file picker opens by itself.

Account/Password, Everyday (name, phone, email, address), Card, and Secure note — with subtypes for scripts, keys, recovery codes and config files. Account and Everyday entries also take unlimited custom fields, encrypted just like the built-in ones.

Settings → Enable autofill → pick Sekuvo from the system list. The list is called “Passwords, passkeys & autofill → Preferred service” on Samsung and Android 14+, and “Autofill service” on stock Android.\nAfter that, tapping a sign-in or card field offers your entries. While the vault is locked the system is handed nothing at all.

Settings → Enable the keyboard, then pick “Sekuvo Keyboard” from the keyboard switcher when you need it. It types stored values straight into any field, with search and recents on top. While locked it shows only entries you marked for quick access.
Typing into a computer over Bluetooth

First time? Settings → Bluetooth setup wizard walks you through every step live.
Open the entry, tap the 💻 icon next to the field and KEEP THAT SCREEN OPEN — the phone only announces itself as a keyboard while it is. On the computer, add the phone as a new Bluetooth device and confirm the code. Back on the phone pick your computer, choose THE COMPUTER’S keyboard layout, click into the target field and tap Type.
Connected but nothing is typed? The computer paired your phone as a phone earlier, so it never enabled the keyboard service. Remove the pairing on BOTH sides, open the 💻 screen, and pair again starting from the computer. On Windows a “Bluetooth HID” device should then appear under Device Manager → Human Interface Devices. On macOS, dismiss the Keyboard Setup Assistant if it opens.
Use the speed test as a diagnostic: nothing typed means pairing, garbled characters mean the layout, a cut-off run means the speed.
The vault locks the moment the screen it is on goes dark — folding a foldable counts. Leaving the app while the screen stays on does not lock it: the app, the keyboard and autofill share one session.

System backup is off by design, so your vault leaves the phone exactly one way: Settings → Create encrypted backup. Use a backup password different from your master password. The resulting .vaultbak file plus that password restores everything on any phone, even after a factory reset.

The ➕ button offers “Import via QR” and “Import from text”. The ⇄ wizard does both in one flow: it generates a single-use transfer password, types it into the computer over Bluetooth, and then takes the envelope back either by scanning the QR or from the clipboard — decrypting it with that same password.\nThe computer-side tool is a download, not a website: get aktar.html from the project’s Releases page, check its SHA-256, and open it from your own disk. This site never asks you for a secret.
Check the address — it needs an @ and a domain like example.com
Enter the month and year as MMYY (month 01–12)
This IBAN\'s check digits do not match — a digit is probably mistyped
This IBAN\'s check digits do not match, so a digit is probably wrong. You can still save it — but if it was a typo, you will not notice until the transfer fails.

The SHA-256 of the computer-side tool, aktar.html. This is not a secret — it is the reference you measure a downloaded file against. Keep it here, check it before you open the file, and refresh it when a new version comes out.
Scan the encrypted envelope holding the new anchor, then enter the transfer password you set on the computer.
Kept when the password changes, with the date it was replaced. Tap the eye to reveal one.
Scan the encrypted envelope holding the new password, then enter the transfer password you set on the computer. Only the password is taken; nothing is added to the vault.
The envelope opened but carries no usable value.
The menus on the computer differ by system, so I\'ll show you the right path.
The phone will appear to the computer as a keyboard. That takes three things:
Permission was not given. Turn on “Nearby devices” in the app settings.
The phone is ready as a keyboard
Taking long? Turn Bluetooth off and on again.
This phone is already paired with a computer. What would you like to do?
Pick your computer from the list:
Not in the list — pair a new one
On the computer, your phone will appear under this name:
Start → Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Add device → Bluetooth (Windows 10: Settings → Devices → Add Bluetooth or other device)
Apple menu → System Settings → Bluetooth (System Preferences on older versions). Keep the window open.
Settings → Bluetooth (on KDE: System Settings → Bluetooth → Add new device)
The corner with the clock → Bluetooth → Pair new device
Start a Bluetooth search on the computer (%1$s)
You need to do this yourself

Sekuvo can\'t make the phone visible on its own. Open the phone\'s Bluetooth settings with the button below and, if you see it, tap “Pair new device”: the phone is visible only while that pairing screen is open. As soon as your phone\'s name appears in the computer\'s list, come straight back to this screen — while Sekuvo is in the background, the computer can\'t see the phone as a keyboard.
With this screen open, click your phone\'s name on the computer. If the same code appears on both screens, confirm on BOTH sides.
✓ You\'re back in Sekuvo — now click your phone\'s name on the computer.
If the Keyboard Setup Assistant opens on the Mac, close it.
Waiting for the computer to pair…
The computer may have paired this phone earlier as a phone, not as a keyboard. Remove the pairing on BOTH sides (phone and computer), keep this screen open, and pair again starting from the computer.
On the computer, open Notepad (type “notepad” in Start) and put the cursor in it.
On the computer, open TextEdit (⌘ + Space → TextEdit) and put the cursor in a new document.
On the computer, open a text editor (e.g. Text Editor, Kate) and put the cursor in it.
On the computer, open any text field (e.g. a note or a document) and put the cursor in it.
Exactly this should appear on the computer:
The layout is wrong: pick your computer\'s layout above, delete the text on the computer and try again.
Make sure the cursor is in a text field on the computer. If still nothing appears, remove the pairing on both sides and run the wizard again.
From now on, open an entry and tap the 💻 next to a field: %1$s will be at the top of the list.
Computer not listed or not connecting? Open the setup wizard
Set up typing to the computer now
Your vault lives on this phone
Everything is encrypted with a key derived from your master password. Sekuvo has no internet permission: your data goes nowhere.
Accounts and passwords, everyday details, cards and secure notes. Add as many fields as you like to an entry; password fields stay hidden.
The Sekuvo Keyboard types a value straight into the field, and autofill suggests your entries on login forms. Turn both on in Settings.
Back up on your own terms
Save an encrypted .vaultbak backup wherever you like. The file and its password bring everything back, even on a new phone.
Type on your computer like a keyboard
The phone connects to the computer as a Bluetooth keyboard and types the password key by key where the cursor is. Nothing is installed on the computer. Let\'s set it up together, live.
